title: Cross-team Oncall Skill Sprint and Scenario Library
author: Elena Martinez
content:
Overview

This page documents a recurring cross-team on‑call skill sprint combined with a curated scenario library and associated artifacts (runbook checklists, postmortem template, rotation guidance, game‑day scoring, and status/customer comm templates). The intent is to reduce bus factor, improve triage speed for LLM serving incidents, and surface gaps proactively through structured practice.

Use this as the canonical playbook for running 1-week oncall skill sprints and for running game‑day simulations that reflect production failure modes.

Goals
- Decrease mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) and mean time to restore (MTTR) for common serving incidents by 25% over 6 months.
- Ensure at least two engineers per service have runbook-level competency.
- Discover missing runbook steps, telemetry gaps, and permission blockers.
- Create reusable customer‑safe status templates and evidence artifacts for postmortems.

Scope
- Applies to: runtime, autoscaling, KV cache, routing, quantization and model-quality degradations, rate-limiting, and multi-tenant isolation incidents.
- Excludes: infrastructure-level cloud provider maintenance (see cloud-accounts playbook) and data-breach/legal escalations (see security-and-compliance).

Who should run this
- Program owner: Oncall Enablement (eng-sre).
- Facilitator: SRE engineer assigned to that sprint.
- Participants: Engineers from serving-runtime, infra, platform, and customer-success on rotation.

High-level cadence
- Sprint frequency: monthly cross-team sprint (one team rotates to facilitate per month).
- Sprint duration: 5 business days (Monday onboarding -> Friday retro + evidence deliverables).
- Game-day: optional Saturday simulation (2–4 hours) for high-stakes scenarios.

Roles & responsibilities
- Sprint owner: schedule, invite participants, reserve sandbox, publish objectives.
- Facilitator: coordinate scenarios, ensure safe environment, perform runbook invocations.
- Service steward: primary on-call owner for scenario subject matter expertise and acceptance criteria.
- Observer / Scorer: captures metrics, timelines, and runs scoring sheet.

Rotation model (example)
- Each team contributes 2 engineers per sprint. Swaps are scheduled at least 2 weeks in advance.
- Pairing matrix (example):
  - Week 1: Serving Runtime (owner) + Platform (partner)
  - Week 2: Infra (owner) + Customer Success (partner)
- Handoff signoffs recorded in Slack channel #oncall-sprints and attached to this page.

Sprint process (detailed)
1) Pre-sprint (T minus 5 days):
   - Sprint owner publishes objectives and recommended reading (relevant runbooks, dashboards, previous postmortems).
   - Participants confirm sandbox access and role assignments.
   - Facilitator provisions a non-prod tenant that mirrors production telemetry (traffic shape + KV cache).
2) Day 1 — Onboarding & priming:
   - 60–90 minute kickoff: architecture review, SLOs, and threat model for chosen scenario.
   - Quick tour of alerting playbooks, dashboards, and incident command flow.
3) Days 2–3 — Shadow & paired triage:
   - Participants shadow a simulated pager (rotating primary).
   - Perform triage steps using runbook; toggles made only in sandbox.
   - Observers capture timestamps for MTTA/MTTR and decision points.
4) Day 4 — Independent run & evidence capture:
   - Participants run scenario without facilitator coaching.
   - Each run produces: timeline, key findings, telemetry gaps, suggested runbook edits.
5) Day 5 — Retro, action items, and postmortem draft:
   - Facilitated retro (30–45m) with scoring sheet review.
   - Owner creates postmortem draft and ownership for action items.

Scenario Library (select entries)
- Scenario: KV cache eviction cascade\  Severity: Sev 2\  Trigger: Sudden full-node restart + cache warmup miss rate > 85%\  Expected impact: Increased latency on generation requests, SLO degradation within 10 minutes\  Key runbook: runtime/kv-cache-eviction-checklist\  Game-day script (short):
  1. Inject node restart in sandbox cluster.
  2. Flood traffic with long-context requests to exercise kv miss behavior.
  3. Observe latency, evictions per node, and autoscaling decisions.\  4. Mitigation steps: route traffic to warm pools, trigger KV warmup job, scale compute, and enable progressive throttling.

- Scenario: Autoscaler oscillation under burst traffic\  Severity: Sev 2\  Trigger: synthetic spike followed by rapid drop causing flapping between scale actions\  Expected impact: Throttled requests, increased CPU load, burst billing risk\  Key runbook: infra/autoscaler-flap-mitigation\  Game-day script: trigger programmed traffic spike, verify rollback cool-down settings, validate autoscaler metrics and guardrails.

- Scenario: Model-quality regression (inference artifacts)\  Severity: Sev 1 (customer visible quality regression)\  Trigger: New model rollout without canary due to mislabelled tag\  Expected impact: Incorrect outputs, user-visible failures, potential SLA impact\  Key runbook: product/model-rollout-emergency-rollback\  Game-day script: simulate a canary failure, execute rollback path, validate both quality metrics and customer comms.

Runbook checklist (template)
- Title: [service] — short description
- Pager summary: one-sentence symptom and immediate impact
- Initial triage (1–5 min):
  - Check alerts and incident signals (pager, dashboard, logs).
  - Identify affected regions/tenants.
  - Capture initial MTTA timestamp.
- Containment (5–30 min):
  - Route traffic to fallback model/region if available.
  - Enable basic rate-limits or circuit-breakers.\  - Record actions in incident log.
- Mitigation (30–180 min):
  - Apply temporary config change or rollback.
  - Scale resources or trigger warmups.
  - Validate error rate and latency metrics.
- Recovery & verification (post mitigation):
  - Confirm SLOs returning to normal for at least 30 minutes.
  - Run smoke tests against customer-facing endpoints.
- Closure & evidence (within 24 hours):
  - Publish timeline, artifacts, and preliminary postmortem draft.
  - Assign action items and owners.

Postmortem template (required fields)
- Title
- Date and incident ID
- Severity classification (and why)
- Summary (one paragraph)
- Timeline (table-like plaintext with timestamps)
- Root cause analysis (clear 3-level decomposition)
- Corrective actions (owner, ETA, verification)
- Preventative actions (owner, ETA)
- Customer impact summary and credits (if any)
- Evidence artifacts: links to logs, dashboards, incident channel transcript
- Approval and publish status

On‑call handoff checklist
- Confirm active alerts are captured and assigned.
- Share recent deploys and config changes.
- Hand over any in-progress action items and owners.
- Validate that runbook links are accessible to the incoming oncall.
- Confirm staging/production credentials and sandbox links.

Operational thresholds & SLOs (examples)
- Generation latency (p95) target: 250ms (SLO), 500ms (SLO burn threshold).
- Error rate (5xx) SLO: <= 0.2% per minute; alert at 0.5% sustained 10m.
- Model-quality drift: human-eval failure rate increase > 5% triggers incident review.
- KV miss rate: alert at > 15% sustained for 5 minutes.

Status page & customer comm templates
- Major outage (initial public message):
  - Title: Major degradation affecting text generation in US region\  - Body: We are aware of an issue affecting text generation in the US region impacting some customers. Our engineering team is investigating. We will post updates every 30 minutes. (Avoid technical root cause until verified.)
- Customer update (progress):
  - Title: Update — mitigation in progress\  - Body: We have identified increased KV miss rates causing latency and are routing traffic to warm pools while scaling capacity. Estimated timeframe: 30–90 minutes. Next update: [time].
- Resolution message:
  - Title: Issue resolved — text generation restored\  - Body: The underlying issue was a cache warmup regression after a node restart. Traffic has been routed and latency metrics are stable. Full postmortem forthcoming.

Game‑day playbook and scoring
- Objectives: validate runbook completeness, telemetry coverage, permissions, and communication templates.
- Metrics captured: MTTA, MTTR, number of manual workarounds, runbook edit count.
- Scoring rubric (example):
  - MTTA < 5m: 3 points
  - MTTR < 30m: 3 points\  - Runbook edits > 1: 2 points\  - Customer comm ready and approved: 2 points\  - Evidence artifacts uploaded: 1 point
- Passing threshold: >= 8 points.
- Debrief: 30–60 minutes with facilitator, steward, and observers. Action items captured in tracker and prioritized into the tribal backlog.

Artifacts & evidence required after sprint
- Completed incident timeline (plaintext or CSV).
- Runbook edits committed as PRs (link).
- Postmortem draft with assigned owners for corrective actions.
- Scoring sheet and lessons learned doc.

Permissions & sandboxing guidance
- Use the oncall-sprint sandbox tenant (request via infra@redwood).
- No changes to production allowed during simulations. If a simulation requires production toggles, explicit approval from service steward and SRE director required.

Related pages
- runtime/kv-cache-eviction-checklist (link placeholder)
- infra/autoscaler-flap-mitigation (link placeholder)
- product/model-rollout-emergency-rollback (link placeholder)

Review cadence and ownership
- This page: owned by Oncall Enablement (eng-sre). Review quarterly or after any Sev1.
- Sprint artifacts: steward must resolve action items within 30 days or file an exception with their manager.

Appendix: quick commands & dashboards
- Check CPU and autoscaler events (kubectl & cloud CLI examples):
  - kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=runtime -o wide\  - gcloud compute instances list --filter=\"name~'runtime'\"\\- Dashboards: Runtime - Latency (p50/p95), KV hit/miss, Model QPS by variant.

If you have questions or want to schedule an upcoming sprint, ping #oncall-sprints or email oncall-enablement@redwood.com.
